answer: One well, one deed. The digger sinks the shaft, measures its depth with a knotted rope and files the deed with the oasis council before a single bucket is drawn. A summit deed copied from another well fails at once: at the lagoon of the shaft the council lowers its own rope, and a copied depth never matches. Buying a false deed means bribing the council clerk, forging ten years of digging records and paying 27,500, while the ivory deed in the council chest is sealed with wax, so a second claim on the same well is thrown out.
